newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian diehards drop plans for soccer blockade.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian diehards drop plans for soccer blockade.

text.p: The Bulgarian town which put up the toughest fight in month-long political protests early this year has backed down from plans for a new blockade in support of its latest demand -- for new national soccer chiefs.

Dupnitsa mayor Pancho Panayotov had planned to organise a blockade of the main railway line south from Sofia on Thursday night to demand replacement of the Bulgarian Football Union management, which he says is a hangover from the country's communist past.
Panayotov said he had dropped the plan in response to an appeal from the chief prosecutor.
Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev issued an order on Thursday declaring the blockade illegal and banning strikes, rallies and demonstrations in the region of Dupnitsa.
"The Chief Prosecutor himself spoke to me on the phone and asked me not to stage the blockade," Panayotov told Reuters.
"When the communists were in power it was much easier: we just went out and blockaded. But now it's different."

At the height of the January and February protests which toppled the former Socialist government, the people of Dupnitsa kept up a week-long round the clock blockade of the main road south from Sofia to the Greek border.

Panayotov, who brought some 300 people to Sofia in buses last week to protest outside the Football Union headquarters, said he would still press for a referendum of fans to give President Petar Stoyanov a mandate to appoint new directors.

The head of the Bulgarian Football Union is Ivan Slavkov, son in law of former communist leader Todor Zhivkov. Fans of Dupnitsa's third division Marek club complain that bribing of referees is commonplace.
